investigational_plan.markdown:
# 1.20 General Investigational Plan - POC Draft

Case: IND001

## Rationale for the drug and the research
AVC-101 is an oral small-molecule inhibitor intended to address the limited treatment options for participants with recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, a tumour type that responds poorly to conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy. Nonclinical studies support an acceptable margin between the pharmacologically active exposure and exposures associated with toxicity.

## Indication to be studied
recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer

## General approach to evaluating the drug
Development will proceed sequentially. A first-in-human dose-escalation study will characterise safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics and identify a recommended dose. Expansion at that dose will provide a preliminary assessment of antitumour activity before any decision to proceed to a randomised study.

## Kinds of clinical trials planned for the first year
One Phase 1 dose-escalation study with a dose-expansion component is planned in the first year following submission. No additional clinical studies are planned during that period.

## Estimated number of participants
Approximately 36 participants (up to 24 in dose escalation and 12 in dose expansion).

## Anticipated risks of particular severity or seriousness
Based on repeat-dose toxicology in rat and dog, the anticipated risks of particular severity are reversible hepatocellular injury observed at exposures above the proposed starting dose, and dose-dependent neutropenia. Liver function tests and absolute neutrophil counts are protocol-specified stopping criteria.

## Studies planned for the first year

### 1. A Phase 1 Study of AVC-101 in Participants with Recurrent Low-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer
- **Objectives:** To determine the safety, tolerability and maximum tolerated dose of oral AVC-101; to characterise single- and multiple-dose pharmacokinetics; to make a preliminary assessment of antitumour activity.
- **Study design:** Open-label, single-arm, 3+3 dose escalation followed by dose expansion at the recommended dose.
- **Planned sample size:** Up to 36 participants; no formal sample size calculation was performed for this preliminary study.
- **Study population:** Adults with histologically confirmed recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer who have received at least one prior line of systemic therapy.
- **Study parameters:** Safety and tolerability by adverse events, laboratory tests, ECG and physical examination. Pharmacokinetic parameters include Cmax, Tmax and AUC. Antitumour activity assessed by RECIST v1.1.
- **Status:** Protocol submitted with this Initial IND. Enrolment has not started.

_Required elements follow 21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)(iv). POC draft from synthetic data; not submission-ready._

fields.plan.rationale: RNV-220 is an inhaled agent intended to provide once-daily control of moderate persistent asthma with lower systemic exposure than currently available oral therapy. Nonclinical inhalation toxicology supports evaluation in humans at the proposed doses.
fields.plan.general_approach: A first-in-human study in healthy adult volunteers will establish safety, tolerability and systemic exposure following single and repeat inhaled doses before any study is conducted in participants with asthma.
fields.plan.first_year_scope: One Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose study in healthy adult volunteers is planned in the first year. A patient study is contemplated thereafter but its protocol has not been developed.
fields.plan.estimated_enrollment: Approximately 48 healthy adult volunteers across all dose cohorts.
fields.plan.anticipated_risks: Anticipated risks of particular severity are bronchospasm following inhaled administration and, at the highest planned doses, the systemic corticosteroid-like effects seen in 13-week dog inhalation toxicology. Spirometry is performed before and after each dose, and rescue medication is available at the site.

investigational_plan.markdown:
# 1.20 General Investigational Plan - POC Draft

Case: IND004

## Rationale for the drug and the research
RNV-220 is an inhaled agent intended to provide once-daily control of moderate persistent asthma with lower systemic exposure than currently available oral therapy. Nonclinical inhalation toxicology supports evaluation in humans at the proposed doses.

## Indication to be studied
moderate persistent asthma

## General approach to evaluating the drug
A first-in-human study in healthy adult volunteers will establish safety, tolerability and systemic exposure following single and repeat inhaled doses before any study is conducted in participants with asthma.

## Kinds of clinical trials planned for the first year
One Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose study in healthy adult volunteers is planned in the first year. A patient study is contemplated thereafter but its protocol has not been developed.

## Estimated number of participants
Approximately 48 healthy adult volunteers across all dose cohorts.

## Anticipated risks of particular severity or seriousness
Anticipated risks of particular severity are bronchospasm following inhaled administration and, at the highest planned doses, the systemic corticosteroid-like effects seen in 13-week dog inhalation toxicology. Spirometry is performed before and after each dose, and rescue medication is available at the site.

## Studies planned for the first year

### 1. A Phase 1 Study of RNV-220 in Healthy Adult Volunteers
- **Objectives:** To evaluate the safety and tolerability of single and multiple ascending inhaled doses of RNV-220 and to characterise systemic pharmacokinetics.
- **Study design:** Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single- and multiple-ascending-dose study.
- **Planned sample size:** Approximately 48 participants, 8 per cohort randomised 6:2 active to placebo.
- **Study population:** Healthy adults aged 18 to 55 with normal spirometry and no history of reactive airway disease.
- **Study parameters:** Adverse events, spirometry, vital signs, ECG, clinical laboratory tests, and plasma pharmacokinetics.
- **Status:** Protocol submitted with this Initial IND. Enrolment has not started.

fields.plan.rationale:
Mechanism of action: Simultaneous engagement of PRAME_peptide/HLA-A*02:01 on tumor and CD3epsilon on T cells -> polyclonal T-cell activation, granzyme/perforin-mediated lysis, IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha/IL-2 release, T-cell proliferation.

Class precedent: Pr20 TCRm antibody (Chang et al., Nat Med 2017, PMC5490756); IMA402 TCER PRAME x CD3 (NCT05958121, Immatics); IMA203 TCR-T (Wermke et al., Nat Med 2025).

Starting-dose rationale: Modified-MABEL: 0.5 microg flat (~0.0075 microg/kg in 70-kg subject) yields projected Cmax ~ 0.041 ng/mL, ~3x below the in vitro EC10 (0.12 ng/mL) for tumor-cell lysis and >= 100x below the lowest concentration producing measurable IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha release.
fields.plan.general_approach:
Dose-escalation approach: modified mTPI-2 with accelerated titration lead-in, target DLT rate 30%, equivalence interval [0.25-0.35]

Dose levels: mTPI-2 with accelerated titration lead-in. Dose levels (microg flat): -1=0.25, 1=0.5, 2=1.5, 3=3, 4=5, 5=10, 6=20, 7=40, 8=80, 9=160 (MTD/RP2D estimate).

Step-up priming: C1D1 0.5 microg -> C1D8 5 microg -> C2D1 onwards target cohort dose, with CRS/ICANS pre-med and 48-h in-patient observation for the first dose at each new step-up.

Premedication: Acetaminophen 650 mg PO + diphenhydramine 25 mg PO + dexamethasone 8 mg IV 4-6 h before each step-up dose; cytoreduction not required.
fields.plan.first_year_scope:
Study design: open-label, single-agent, dose-escalation + expansion, 21-day cycles, once-weekly IV dosing, mandatory step-up priming C1D1 0.5 ug / C1D8 5 ug

Number of sites: 4-6

Planned duration: escalation ~24 months, treatment <= 24 months per subject
fields.plan.estimated_enrollment: up to 50: <= 30 Part A + ~20 Part B
fields.plan.anticipated_risks: The anticipated risks of PMX-103 in the clinical study are: (i) cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which is a class effect of T-cell engagers and is anticipated based on the nonclinical findings; (ii) immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) and other neurologic events; (iii) infusion-related reactions; (iv) hematologic toxicity, including lymphopenia and cytopenias; (v) hepatic transaminase elevations; (vi) infections, including opportunistic infections; and (vii) immunogenicity (ADA). These risks will be mitigated through the mandatory step-up priming schedule, premedication, in-patient observation during the first dose at each new step-up, intensive safety monitoring, and the CRS/ICANS management algorithm described in the protocol.

investigational_plan.markdown:
# 1.20 General Investigational Plan - POC Draft

Case: PMX103

## Rationale for the drug and the research
Mechanism of action: Simultaneous engagement of PRAME_peptide/HLA-A*02:01 on tumor and CD3epsilon on T cells -> polyclonal T-cell activation, granzyme/perforin-mediated lysis, IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha/IL-2 release, T-cell proliferation.

Class precedent: Pr20 TCRm antibody (Chang et al., Nat Med 2017, PMC5490756); IMA402 TCER PRAME x CD3 (NCT05958121, Immatics); IMA203 TCR-T (Wermke et al., Nat Med 2025).

Starting-dose rationale: Modified-MABEL: 0.5 microg flat (~0.0075 microg/kg in 70-kg subject) yields projected Cmax ~ 0.041 ng/mL, ~3x below the in vitro EC10 (0.12 ng/mL) for tumor-cell lysis and >= 100x below the lowest concentration producing measurable IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha release.

## Indication to be studied
Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors that are (i) PRAME-positive (central IHC H-score >= 80) AND (ii) HLA-A*02:01-positive, after >= 1 prior line of standard therapy including a PD-(L)1 inhibitor where indicated.

## General approach to evaluating the drug
Dose-escalation approach: modified mTPI-2 with accelerated titration lead-in, target DLT rate 30%, equivalence interval [0.25-0.35]

Dose levels: mTPI-2 with accelerated titration lead-in. Dose levels (microg flat): -1=0.25, 1=0.5, 2=1.5, 3=3, 4=5, 5=10, 6=20, 7=40, 8=80, 9=160 (MTD/RP2D estimate).

Step-up priming: C1D1 0.5 microg -> C1D8 5 microg -> C2D1 onwards target cohort dose, with CRS/ICANS pre-med and 48-h in-patient observation for the first dose at each new step-up.

Premedication: Acetaminophen 650 mg PO + diphenhydramine 25 mg PO + dexamethasone 8 mg IV 4-6 h before each step-up dose; cytoreduction not required.

## Kinds of clinical trials planned for the first year
Study design: open-label, single-agent, dose-escalation + expansion, 21-day cycles, once-weekly IV dosing, mandatory step-up priming C1D1 0.5 ug / C1D8 5 ug

Number of sites: 4-6

Planned duration: escalation ~24 months, treatment <= 24 months per subject

## Estimated number of participants
up to 50: <= 30 Part A + ~20 Part B

## Anticipated risks of particular severity or seriousness
The anticipated risks of PMX-103 in the clinical study are: (i) cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which is a class effect of T-cell engagers and is anticipated based on the nonclinical findings; (ii) immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) and other neurologic events; (iii) infusion-related reactions; (iv) hematologic toxicity, including lymphopenia and cytopenias; (v) hepatic transaminase elevations; (vi) infections, including opportunistic infections; and (vii) immunogenicity (ADA). These risks will be mitigated through the mandatory step-up priming schedule, premedication, in-patient observation during the first dose at each new step-up, intensive safety monitoring, and the CRS/ICANS management algorithm described in the protocol.

## Studies planned for the first year

### 1. Phase 1 Clinical Study Protocol for PMX-103 (PMX-103-P1-001)
- **Study design:** open-label, single-agent, dose-escalation + expansion, 21-day cycles, once-weekly IV dosing, mandatory step-up priming C1D1 0.5 ug / C1D8 5 ug
- **Planned sample size:** up to 50: <= 30 Part A + ~20 Part B
- **Study population:** Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors that are (i) PRAME-positive (central IHC H-score >= 80) AND (ii) HLA-A*02:01-positive, after >= 1 prior line of standard therapy including a PD-(L)1 inhibitor where indicated.
- **Status:** Protocol v3.0 dated 22 August 2026. Enrolment has not started.

invariant_scan.method: Candidate sentences are located deterministically by anchoring on the parameter's name. A model then judges each sentence in isolation - does this sentence assert a value for this parameter - and reports the value verbatim without converting it. The comparison against the declared value, including unit normalisation, is done in code afterwards. The model never generates a number and never decides whether two numbers match.
invariant_scan.note: CONSISTENT means every sentence found asserting this parameter states the declared value. INCONSISTENT means at least one states something else. INCOMPLETE means a sentence sets out to state the parameter and carries no readable value - a hole in the document rather than a contradiction. UNSUPPORTED means no sentence was judged to assert it at all, which is not the same as the value being wrong. Text invariants are not scanned.
